title: We Are What We Remember: Mental-State-Driven Memory for Long-Term Character Dialogue
abstract: arXiv:2611.16223v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Shared history in human dialogue is not merely a repository of facts, but the foundation of evolving relationships and mutual understanding. However, mainstream conversational memory systems rely on passive semantic similarity over external fact stores, frequently retrieving topically similar records while missing relationally pivotal experiences. Inspired by cognitive psychology's Self-Memory System (SMS), we propose MindMem, a mental-state-driven memory framework that asynchronously consolidates shared experiences into source-linked mental states of the character, the user, and their relationship. At each turn, a specialized mental-state reasoner (Mind) contextualizes these persistent states to anticipate latent user needs, form proactive intentions, and recover supporting episodic evidence that surface-level matching overlooks. translated_title: 我们即我们的记忆：面向长期角色对话的心理状态驱动记忆
translated_abstract: 人类对话中的共同历史不仅仅是一个事实存储库，更是不断演进的关系与相互理解的基础。然而，主流的对话记忆系统依赖于对外部事实库的被动语义相似度检索，经常检索到主题相似的记录，却遗漏了在关系层面至关重要的经历。受认知心理学中自我记忆系统（Self-Memory System, SMS）的启发，我们提出了MindMem——一个由心理状态驱动的记忆框架，它能够异步地将共同经历整合为与源头关联的、关于角色、用户以及二者关系的心理状态。在每一轮对话中，一个专门的心理状态推理器（Mind）会结合这些持续存在的心理状态，以预测用户潜在的需求、形成主动的意图，并找回表层匹配所忽视的支持性情节证据。为了评估超越事实回忆的历史敏感适应性，我们引入了MemReal-Bench，这是一个纵向（摘要内容在此处被截断）
tldr: 提出受认知心理学自我记忆系统启发的MindMem框架，通过异步将共同经历整合为角色、用户及关系的心理状态来驱动主动式记忆推理与用户需求预测，并引入MemReal-Bench基准评估超越事实回忆的历史敏感对话适应性。
en_tdlr: We propose MindMem, a cognitive-psychology-inspired framework that asynchronously consolidates shared experiences into mental states of the character, user, and relationship to drive proactive reasoning and anticipate latent user needs, and introduce MemReal-Bench to evaluate history-sensitive dialogue adaptation beyond factual recall.
